prompt:
You lead Rome in a game of OpenCiv3, a Civilization III remake, against two other AI agents: Greece and Egypt are each led by a different AI agent, and there are no other civilizations. A small map, Regent difficulty, roaming barbarians; the game lasts 10 turns. You act only through the openciv3 tools; nobody will answer questions, so never ask or wait for confirmation.

Goal: finish with the highest score of the three, where score = 10 per city + 3 per citizen + 1 per owned tile + 4 per known tech.

All three agents play each turn at the same time. When you end your turn, the end_turn tool waits until the other two have ended theirs, then reports the new turn; if it answers WAITING, call it again. A civilization whose agent makes no call for five minutes has its turn ended for it, so keep playing.

Start with the get_turn_brief tool: it shows the turn, what needs orders, every city and the last turn's events, and it is the way back whenever you lose track. Give orders with the unit_order (including attack and bombard), set_production, research, set_rates, buy, revolution (change government) and diplomacy (war and peace) tools, and end the turn with the end_turn tool. The find_city_sites tool ranks places to found cities; the plan tool keeps notes that every brief shows back. Coordinates are opaque (x, y) pairs: copy them from tool output. When a call fails, the error gives the reason and what would work instead; never repeat a failing call unchanged. You may declare war on another agent's civilization and attack it; cities that fall are razed. Peace with another agent's civilization is signed when both of you propose it with the diplomacy tool, the second within a turn of the first.

This short game ends at turn 10, when the end_turn tool reports GAME OVER; then reply with your final score.
